analysis: Examined head lines 1-915 of ClusterOnboardingLive.swift (onboarding wiring, forwarded control channel, link setup, pairing, service install, planning). The visible changes are: new closures stopsAsked and serveUnlessStopped (lines 77-78); execute() now returns followerStatus(reply), which adds start progress and stopsAsked to status replies (lines 399-408); forwarded .serve passes request.stopsBefore into localServe(unlessStoppedSince:) and .stop calls localStop(asked: true) (lines 464-465). These are the boundary between a cable-paired peer and the leader (the pairing and link exchange are authenticated, see line 769). The forwarded request is decoded by the same ClusterControl channel that already carried serve and stop. Within the supplied text I see no new authentication bypass, no data exposure beyond a stop counter and progress, and no connection to the TB-002/TB-011 provider-to-coordinator authorization path, the keys (A-002, A-003), or prompt data. The counter and stop-since semantics only gate whether a start proceeds, so the worst case is a paired peer (already authorized to stop and start) suppressing or racing a serve, which is an availability matter within the existing trust (A-018, no specific threat ID). The implementations of stopsAsked, currentStopsAsked, localServe(unlessStoppedSince:), localStop(asked:) and the later changed ranges (about lines 1459-2597) were not in the supplied units, so the persistence, validation and bounds of the stop counter and the ordering and TOCTOU behavior of serve-unless-stopped are unverified. The patch excerpt is truncated. A next pass should check that the stopsBefore comparison fails safe on malformed or absent values (older peers), that the stop record is stored owner-only through ClusterSetupStore, and that the replies stay bounded.
